title: Count & Conquer
subtitle: ShopIndia needs numbers, not just names
conceptSummary: Aggregate functions summarize many rows into one number: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX.

dialogue.text: ShopIndia's CFO wants the total revenue and average transaction amount. One number each. No long lists!
Aggregate functions. COUNT rows, SUM values, AVG for average. These turn many rows into one number.

teachMoment.title: Aggregate Functions
teachMoment.body:
Summarize data with:
• COUNT(*) — how many rows?
• SUM(column) — total of a number column
• AVG(column) — average value
• MIN(column) — smallest value
• MAX(column) — largest value

Example: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(total_amount), AVG(total_amount) FROM transactions

task.instruction: Find the total number of completed transactions, total revenue (SUM of total_amount), and average transaction amount for completed transactions.
task.startingQuery:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_transactions,
       SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue,
       AVG(total_amount) AS avg_amount
FROM transactions
WHERE status = 'completed'
task.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_transactions, SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_amount FROM transactions WHERE status = 'completed'

hints.text: You need COUNT(*) for count, SUM(total_amount) for revenue, AVG(total_amount) for average.
Add WHERE status = 'completed' to only count completed transactions.
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_transactions, SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_amount FROM transactions WHERE status = 'completed'

winDialogue.text: 22 completed transactions, total ₹1.5 lakhs, average ₹6,800. The CFO is happy!
Now break it down by customer. Which customers are spending the most? GROUP BY is the next tool.

storyBeat: Revenue numbers look normal on the surface. But broken down by customer, one person's spending pattern is wildly inconsistent with their reported income. We need GROUP BY.
